thread_text:
Maya: Quick idea 1: show a p95 confidence band (shaded area) on the route heatmap instead of a single line. That makes uncertainty visible while sampling is on. Screenshot: https://redwood-internal.screens/conf-band.png
Priya: Love that. Concern: the band could obscure hotspots in the heatmap. Maybe reduce opacity or only show the band on hover/focus.
Leo: Interaction suggestion: default collapsed (thin outline) + expand band on hover or when you toggle "Show confidence". Keyboard: Enter to expand when focused.
Janet: Accessibility nit: ensure the band fill contrasts with adjacent colors. If contrast < 4.5:1, switch to a patterned fill (dot/hatch). Also provide an accessible label: `aria-label="p95 confidence band"`.
Maya: Copy tweak for control: instead of "Show band" use "Show p95 confidence band (est.)" and tooltip: "Estimated range of tail latency based on sample rate." Short hover: "p95 estimate (sampling affects accuracy)".
Priya: For small-multiples, default to per-panel scaling but include a persistent header action: "Align Y" that keeps panels synced if users want to compare magnitudes.
Leo: Edge-case: if sample rate <8% show inline microcopy next to the band toggle: "Low sample 1%   accuracy limited" and disable expand-on-hover to avoid false precision.
DesignBot: CSS hint: `.p95-band{ fill: rgba(60,130,240,0.12); stroke: rgba(60,130,240,0.9); stroke-width:1px; }` Consider adding `background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.06) 0 4px, transparent 4px 8px)` for low-contrast fallback.
Janet: Timepicker keyboard nits: support arrow keys to nudge by current granularity, plus `[` and `]` to jump to preset ranges. Make focus order logical: presets -> manual inputs -> apply.
Maya: UX polish: when toggling sampling modes, show a subtle ephemeral banner: "Display adjusted for sampling confidence" rather than a full toast.
Priya: I'll update the figma frames with the patterned fill and microcopy. ETA 3pm PT. Maya/Leo please review once posted.
Maya: Will review after standup. :eyes:
Leo: Thanks  I'll try keyboard prototypes tonight and add tests for screen-reader announcements.
